conservation.notes: Delisted from the US Endangered Species List on 2007-08-09 after recovery; numbers rose substantially from 1966 to 2015 and it now nests in every continental US state.

human_tolerance.notes: Nests in large estuaries and even in secluded groves inside major cities, and increasingly on human-made reservoirs stocked with fish; adult birds are famously tolerant of people, so flight_distance_m is large.

phases.name: nesting
phases.note: Pair formation, egg laying and incubation in a huge stick nest in a mature tree near open water; the male usually brings the sticks.

phases.name: territorial
phases.note: Fledglings are still being fed in early autumn; northern birds then move south and gather on open lakes and rivers where fish are easy to catch.

vocalizations.description: A high-pitched, drawn-out descending whistle given by both sexes, especially in the winter breeding-season courtship and, where birds gather, over open water.
Rapid, harsh cackling or chittering, given by adults near the nest and by immatures begging for food; the adults also give a guttural 'kee-yer' when a rival is close.

external.note: GBIF usageKey from an EXACT match on the scientific name; iNaturalist taxon id 5305 from the iNaturalist API; ITIS TSN 175420 from the ITISWebService scientific-name search; Wikidata Q127216 from a Wikidata entity search.

conservation.note: IUCN category from Wikidata P141; the delisting year and the 1966-2015 increase from the Wikipedia article.

range.note: Country list derived from 'found in North America' plus the article's breeding range across Alaska, Canada and Mexico; only the three country codes are recorded.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Soars and glides over open water and perches in trees; also walks about a nest.

traits.nest_type.note: 'builds the largest nest of any North American bird ... up to 4 m deep, 2.5 m wide': a huge open stick platform in a mature tree, not a cup or cavity.

traits.mass_kg.note: Midpoint of the two stated sex averages: males 4.1 kg, females as much as 5.6 kg.

traits.wingspan_m.note: Midpoint of 'typical wingspan is between 1.8 and 2.3 m'.

traits.lifespan_y.note: 'The average lifespan of bald eagles in the wild is around 20 years, with the oldest confirmed one having been 38 years of age.'

traits.diet.note: Wikipedia: breeding habitat is open water 'with an abundance of fish', the crop can hold 1 kg, and eagles also take carrion and other birds. 0.75/0.15/0.10 is a judgement that puts fish firmly first but keeps the scavenging and bird-tagging the shared predator program needs.

traits.social.note: Monogamous pairs hold a territory and share a nest; groups of well over a dozen gather to feed and roost, so group_size is recorded as a pair.

traits.defense.note: Authored: an adult eagle leaves a person and circles rather than standing its ground.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement. Wikipedia records birds nesting in groves inside major cities and hunting stocked reservoirs without disturbance, so it is low for a large raptor but not zero.

habitat.use.note: Much of the year is spent soaring and gliding over open water, with a large share perched in trees; upland wintering birds spend time on the ground. Authored split.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Roosts in tall trees near water.

habitat.resources.note: Fish and other vertebrates as prey, carrion when fishing is poor, and a huge stick platform plus high perches from the article. The schema's tag set has no `fish` tag, so `small_vertebrate` carries the fish and waterfowl that make up most of the diet, and `water` is the open water the bird both drinks at and hunts over. `small_vertebrate` and `carrion` are also the two tags fsm-seabird-predator-v1 hunts and scavenges on.

habitat.requires.note: 'Most nests have been found within 200 m of open water' and 'the greatest distance from open water recorded for a bald eagle nest was over 3 km, in Florida'; 3 km is used as the hard placement radius.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Nesting in city estuaries and on stocked reservoirs from Wikipedia; light_max, flight_distance_m and road_mortality are authored.

seasonal.strategy.note: 'northern birds are migratory, while southern birds are resident, remaining on their breeding territory all year'.

seasonal.winter_fraction.note: Judgement, 0.7: the article says northern birds migrate and southern birds are resident but gives no share.

seasonal.phases.note: Nesting-tree and open-water requirements from Wikipedia; the exact month-day boundaries and the autumn territorial window are judgements.

seasonal.life_stages.note: 'Sexual maturity is attained at the age of four to five years' and the immature is dark brown with messy white streaking until the fourth or fifth year; duration_days is 1500, about four years, and scale 0.75 is a judgement for the dark streaked juvenile plumage.

vocalizations.contact.note: The high descending whistle used in courtship and over wintering water; the frequency and duration bands are authored.

vocalizations.alarm.note: The harsh cackling near the nest and the immatures' begging call; the duration band is authored.

look.note: 'evenly dark brown with a white head and tail', 'the beak, feet and irises are bright yellow'; the shaggy white crown is the extra part, and the proportions are authored from the wing chord and tail lengths in the article.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared territorial-predator program. It is nominally a seabird program, but its states - patrol by flight, take live prey, scavenge carrion, drink, retreat from a threat - are what an adult bald eagle does over open water, and it is the closest shared fit. The large flee_m and calm_m reflect the article's tolerance of people.
